note: Lockerbie is on the closed list of 4.6 and the fragment discusses the trial of the suspects and the Council's sanctions.
The sale of children appears only in the title of a protocol, not framed as trafficking (4.7).
Terrorist activities are one item of the quoted series of activities a State may not organize or assist, with no development of their own (3.2, 4.6).
Extremism is not tied to violence (4.6), and peacekeeping and reconciliation are items of an enumeration of efforts with no development of their own (3.2).
The relative clause on arms smuggling spreading crime and violence states a consequence and is a clause of its own, so crime in general counts (3.2, 5.2).
Combating common crime is crime in general, paired with organized crime in a full sentence (5.2).
Domestic and regional forces using violent means to disrupt Iraq's security is a concrete conflict with identifiable parties and place (4.10).
Human smuggling shares the transit claim with drugs and has no fact of its own (3.2).
Calling the State-sponsor designation unfounded and asking for removal concerns the listing, with no terrorism itself discussed (4.6).
The UN's part in the reconciliation process of the speaker's identifiable region is peacebuilding (4.10).
The Programme of Action against the illicit trade in small arms and marking and tracing count for organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
The division of Germany, Korea and Viet-Nam and its settlement by UN-supervised elections are named disputes between rival parties (4.10).
Paired with terrorism in a call for cooperation, 'international crime' means cross-border crime here, not aggression, despite the pre-1990 caution (section 6).
The criminal activities are those of a named terrorist group and are listed by type, so there is no crime in general (5.2).
IUU fishing is named only as an economic threat, and waste discharge as one pollution problem among others (4.8, 5.2).
Peace as a commitment, conflicts with no referent and a threat of force by unnamed great Powers are general invocations (4.10).
Massacres at named places setting back a negotiated settlement in South Africa are a concrete settlement process, beyond the listed regional wars (4.10).
Combating the illicit trade and flow of small arms counts for organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
A full sentence on curbing illicit arms transfers gives organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
Rhodesia is treated as a British colonial matter with sanctions adopted by the United Kingdom; no armed struggle or Security Council measure is named (4.10).
The two world wars are identifiable wars and the subject of a sentence on the use of force and the system governing States (4.10).
Illicit trafficking in light weapons and the conference on the illicit arms trade count for organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
The United Nations' power to impose sanctions on a colonial Power under the Charter is a collective security measure connected with colonialism (4.10).
A full sentence with its own claim on the illicit small-arms trade gives organized_crime (3.2, 4.4).
Wrongful arrests and torture by the police count as police and detention conduct whoever the victims (4.9).
The aggression of extremists against minorities and their beliefs describes no attacks or killings, and extremism is framed as fanaticism and hatred (4.6).
The peace restored in Central America and Colombia is a concrete post-conflict peace and the object of the sentence, not the generic threat formula (4.10, 5.1).
The illicit trade and trafficking in small arms counts for organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
Hindu extremism is tied to the targeting of minorities and the Gujarat massacre, so opposing it counts as violent extremism (4.6).
Regional conflicts, crises and averted threats to peace are mentioned with no identifiable referent (4.10).
Support for resolving ongoing conflicts through UN-sponsored dialogue among political and military forces is mediation, a peace mechanism, though no conflict is named (4.10).
The causes of the crises and conflicts drawn from named regions give the conflicts a referent, so the link claim is not a general invocation (3.2, 4.10).
Transparency in Government contracts through a new National Procurement Authority is a procurement-integrity measure that develops the anti-corruption item (3.2, 4.5).
Preventing and halting armed conflict is stated as the Organization's general task, with no conflict or measure named (4.10).
A full sentence on combating insecurity and crime is about crime in general (5.2).
A sentence about Hamas holding the hostages it took, outside a war between States, gives terrorism (5.2 row a).
The international mission against gang crime in Haiti is a Council-authorized mission (4.10); gang crime appears only in the mission's description and is not developed (3.2).
Compliance with the regional zone-of-peace declaration amid ongoing border and territorial disputes in the region is a concrete matter between States (4.10).
Assisting addicts is one item of a series of measures with no development of its own (3.2).
Drug trafficking is one of two agenda questions introduced together and, unlike the environment, is not developed (3.2).
Safety and insecurity are not tied to crime, police or crime rates in the fragment, and 'this trend' refers outside it (4.5 P3, 5.2).
Drug trafficking is named with terrorism only as examples of the excuses now given, with no development of its own (3.2, 3.3).
The opening sentence claims the link between terrorism in the Sahel and the Libyan crisis, so terrorism counts (3.2).
A full sentence rejecting torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment concerns ill-treatment by officials, counted whoever the victims, though custody is not named (4.9).
A full sentence on preventing arms trafficking gives organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
Crime and criminals appear only as items of repeated series that share one claim, refuge in the United States (3.2, 5.2).
Chairing the meeting on implementing the Programme of Action against the illicit small-arms trade makes that instrument the object of the sentence, not a passing name (3.2, 4.4).
Ending illicit trafficking in small arms is the subject of a full sentence and counts whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
The opening sentence on the growth of violence and crime is about crime in general (5.2).
A full sentence on the illicit trade in small arms gives organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
Kidnapping and torture of civilians in armed conflicts are conflict abuses, not hostage-taking or custody (4.9, 5.2).
The call on Iraq to respect the Khor Abdullah agreements concerns an identifiable dispute between two States (4.10).
Terrorism appears only as an agenda item of regional meetings, each shared with economic goals, with no development of its own (3.2).
Fair-trial guarantees and a judicial request through INTERPOL, with no crime identifiable in the fragment, are courts and cooperation in criminal matters (4.9, 5.1).
The Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine ties international justice to a named aggression, which counts as peace (4.10; YAML criminal_justice exclude).
Civilians held hostage by armed groups for military and political purposes, and their liberation, follow 5.2 row (a), not a ceasefire demand.
Unwanted small-arms flows into the country that cause gun violence are illicit trafficking by kind (4.4, section 1); the threat to peace and security is the formula of 4.10.
The 'economic crimes' and 'criminal activities' are the named looting and illegal exploitation of resources, not economic crime or crime in general (4.5, 4.8, 5.2).
The arms-trafficking and small-arms item is developed by an effect and place of its own, fuelling conflicts in Africa (3.2, 4.4).
Judicial cooperation is set within the drug agenda, and small-arms proliferation is not called illicit (5.1, section 6).
Implementing the Kinshasa Convention to combat the illicit circulation of small arms counts for organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).

The migrant smuggling protocol is negotiated within the Ad Hoc Committee on the Convention against Organized Transnational Crime, linking it to the Palermo Convention (5.1), beyond the listed firearms item.
Extremism is named together with violence as an effect of exclusion and marginalization, which ties it to violence (4.6).
The women, peace and security and protection-of-civilians items are developed with aims of their own, while the crime items are only listed (3.2, 4.10).
Rebuilding the judiciary and the security sector is justice-sector reform (4.9), unlike the transitional and international justice mechanisms.
Transnational networks head the phrase and are the subject of the threat to governments and sovereignty (4.4); the crime is theirs, not crime in general (5.2).
Aggression by a named State and a call for collective action under the OAS Charter is a concrete dispute between States, though the aggression is economic (4.10).
Small arms are framed as disarmament and a scourge, with no illicit trade, trafficking or unauthorized transfer described (4.4, section 6).
Collective action when States fail to protect or harm their populations is protection and collective security, beyond the listed pillars (4.10).
Radicalism is not tied to violence (4.6), while security and defence assistance in the Sahel and restoring State authority concern an identifiable security crisis (4.10).
The risk clause on all kinds of trafficking and criminal activities developing in lawless separatist regions is a clause of its own about crime in general (3.2, 5.2).
Arms proliferation is an arms-control topic however framed, and the sentence claims its link with terrorism, so it is substantive (3.2, 4.10).
A full sentence on combating illegal trafficking in conventional arms gives organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
United Nations efforts to fund and provide security in Haiti amid gang violence are Council-authorized action, which counts as peace without armed conflict (4.10).
The Second World War is a named war and the subject of the sentences on its memory and crimes (4.10).

Money laundering and terrorism are claimed as ramifications of the drug scourge, and the laundering resulting from drug trafficking is an object of the battle, so the link makes both substantive (3.2, 4.5, 5.1).
Demands to remove Sudan from the list of State sponsors of terrorism, with no terrorism itself discussed, give no terrorism (4.6).
Curbing crime, with no type named, is the subject of a sentence linking it to inequality (5.2).
The problem before the First Committee and the aggressors are not identifiable in the fragment (3.2).
Improving judicial procedures is one item of a series of needs with no development of its own; rule of law and impunity after a dictatorship are not ordinary crime (3.2, 4.9).
The call to improve mutual legal assistance and extradition names no crime, so it is cooperation in criminal matters in general (4.9, 5.1), apart from the excluded ICC and tribunals.
Regulating and policing IUU fishing is fisheries management and enforcement, with no criminal groups, prosecution or criminal penalties (4.8).
The larger conflict averted last year is not identifiable in the fragment (3.2).
Standards and controls on the illicit flow of conventional weapons count for organized_crime whoever receives them (4.4).
Boko Haram is on the Security Council's closed list and the fragment discusses the struggle against it, though it calls it an armed group (4.6).
The 'fraudulent and uncontrolled trade in weapons' describes an illicit arms trade by kind, which counts whoever receives the weapons (section 1, 4.4).
The Belgrade conference seeking peaceful coexistence and an end to the spectre of war concerns relations between blocs and the danger of war (4.10).
The sentence's claim is the link between human-trafficking organizations and those managing narco-trafficking, so narco-trafficking is a pole of the link, not a side clause (3.2, 5.1).
The fight against terrorism is the object of an independent clause paired by contrast with the fight against poverty, not an item of an enumeration (3.2).
The armed forces' campaign is described only as resisting Da'esh terrorism, as in example terrorism P2, so peace is not added (4.6, 5.2 row d).
The Security Council debate Belgium organized on illegal exploitation fuelling conflict is Council work on peace and security, beyond the general link (4.10).
Torture and the horrors of the gaols suffered by opponents of apartheid are ill-treatment and conditions of detention, counted whoever the victims (4.9, section 7).
The foreign-bases item is developed with an effect of its own, centres of provocation, subversion and dangerous tensions (3.2, 4.10).

The fraudsters whose customs fraud the reform curbed commit economic crime by individuals, which is corruption (4.5); weapons, ammunition and counterfeit currency are only items of a seizure series (3.2).
After 1990 'international crime' is organized_crime, and the region's headway in fighting it is the main claim of a sentence (5.2; YAML era terms).
The coup and repression in Chile are a domestic overthrow, not a war or an armed conflict between parties, and 'acts of terrorism' is an epithet (4.6, 4.10).
Southern Africa as a potential threat to peace is the formula, and its possible use in a wider political context names no armed struggle, aggression, occupation or Council measure (4.10).
A full sentence on curbing illicit small-arms trafficking gives organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
Suppressing organized crime is one commitment in a series of verb phrases, with no fact or measure of its own (3.2).
The Programme of Action appears with the Ottawa Convention as one of two examples of arms-control progress sharing one evaluation, with no development of its own (3.2, 4.4).
Massacres by forces the speaker calls an extension of Pretoria's army are called terrorism, with a security agreement to end it, so the word is not a mere epithet for an army (4.6, 5.2 row d).
A tribute to martyrs of an unnamed struggle for liberty identifies no war, adversary or place (4.10).
Destroying drug trafficking is one achievement in a series with the return of refugees, with no development of its own (3.2).
Abu Ghraib, Kabul and Aleppo appear only as settings of injustice and humiliation, with no war, party or act discussed (3.2, 4.10).
Asking for Cuba's removal because the classification lacks evidence concerns the listing, with no terrorism itself discussed (4.6).
Miners and logging companies invading indigenous lands are framed as a human-rights violation, with no illegal or criminal framing of the mining or logging itself (4.8).
Young people turning delinquent and engaging in new forms of criminality is crime in general with a claim of its own (5.2, section 8).
Non-alignment's role in reducing international tension and the centres of disturbance, named as the Congo, Cuba, Berlin and nuclear tests, concern bloc tension and concrete crises (4.10).
The difficult situation of detainees in Venezuela concerns detention, counted whoever the detainees (4.9).

The regional framework in step with efforts against the illicit small-arms trade gives organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4); civil unrest and the recent weapons threat identify no armed conflict or disarmament (4.10).
The Conference on the illicit small-arms trade and its enforcement and tracing measures give organized_crime whoever receives the weapons, and no sentence treats a conflict or disarmament (4.4).
Coffee prices and the coffee agreement as factors in drug production are market conditions for the legal products of drug-producing countries (4.3, P2); corruption is one effect in a series (3.2).

The linkage between members of the international financial world and the drug economy is a laundering channel by kind and the object of its sentence (section 1, 4.5); the corruption tied to waste traffic is only participial (5.1).
Rockets and suicide bombs are not called terrorist in the fragment, and bombings count only when so called (4.6).
The notorious drug-trafficking families are criminal organizations and the subject of a sentence on the first strong blow against them, beyond the arrest of one trafficker (4.4, 5.1).
The Security Council's statement on international law and on delisting from its sanctions concerns its sanctions and working methods (4.10).

Transnational organized crime is one threat named with weapons of mass destruction under the threat formula (3.2, 5.1); the clause on conventional arms in the hands of non-State actors, not called illicit, has an actor and a claim of its own and gives peace (3.2, 4.10, section 6).
The assassination of a Head of State abroad by diverting his aircraft, with no perpetrator named as a State's forces, is an attack on an internationally protected person and counts by its kind (4.6).
A UN police force to keep civil order and the training of police for missions concern police as institutions, alongside peacekeeping (4.9).
Calling for Cuba's removal from the 'so-called' list as a Cold War residue concerns the listing, with no terrorism itself discussed (4.6).
Neighbours' accusations that Chinese experts are a Communist army vanguard preparing aggression are a security dispute between identifiable States, framed in bloc terms (4.10).
